data.narrative:
Lilac Solutions, a Series C-stage climate and energy company founded by David Snydacker, has raised $315M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comparable universe of nine private frontier-tech peers and one public company (LNZA), with three direct comparables selected at identical stage and sector: KoBold Metals ($3.0B), Electric Hydrogen ($1.0B), and Amogy ($700M).

Two triangulation methods apply to this stage. Stage-progression analysis, using total capital raised as a proxy baseline, applies a 1.7x multiplier typical of Series C advancement, yielding $536M. Peer-median analysis across the three same-sector, same-stage comparables produces $1.0B, with the peer set spanning $700M to $3.0B. The median peer valuation reflects material dispersion in the sector, indicating stage and capital efficiency alone do not determine value.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $455M (low) to $1.1B (high), with a median of $768M. This 2.4x spread reflects two primary uncertainties: the wide dispersion among direct peers ($700M to $3.0B) and reliance on capital-raise data as a valuation proxy in early-stage, capital-intensive sectors where cash burn and technology risk remain elevated. Revenue data, unit economics, and commercialization milestones would narrow this range materially.
